title: US Flight Chaos Rolls Into Sunday: 6,400 Saturday Cancellations, Normal Only Late Sunday
excerpt: The FAA says schedules should largely recover by late Sunday after Friday's ground stop — the longest since 9/11 — as investigators examine two L3Harris routers and airlines waive rebooking fees.
body:
• US airlines cancelled more than 6,400 flights and delayed over 8,000 on Saturday, after Friday's 9,200 cancellations — and 875 Sunday flights were already cancelled by Saturday night, according to FlightAware figures reported by Reuters.
  • FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said schedules should largely return to normal by late Sunday; the FAA is still testing the network with contractor L3Harris.
  • If your flight is cancelled: Delta, United, American and JetBlue have issued travel waivers allowing rebooking for later dates without extra cost — check your airline's app before heading to the airport.
  • Officials blame a router installed by L3Harris during a copper-to-fibre upgrade; they say there is no evidence of a cyberattack.

The disruption that shut down US air travel on Friday rolled through a second full day on Saturday, and the Federal Aviation Administration says normal schedules will not return until late on Sunday. As of 9:35 p.m. ET on Saturday, airlines had cancelled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware figures reported by Reuters. That followed about 9,200 cancellations and 7,500 delays on Friday, when the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours — the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001 attacks. Another 875 flights scheduled for Sunday had already been cancelled by Saturday night.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He apologised to passengers and said the system remained stable. Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines each cancelled about 25% of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45%, Reuters reported. Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook for later dates without cost, but tens of thousands of travellers were stranded as carriers worked to get aircraft and crews back into position. The disruption even stranded some college football teams on Friday, ahead of games scheduled for Saturday. Our earlier coverage traced the first official account of the router failure and Air India's statement that its US flights ran on schedule during the stop.

Two routers, a flood of connection attempts

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when a router installed by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility — during routine work switching telecommunications lines from copper wiring to fibre-optic infrastructure — began overwhelming the network. "We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy said. The failure affected communications at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centres, which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight. Bedford said the ground stop was ordered as a precaution in case a centre lost all communications: "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost."

"We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was."

— Sean Duffy, US Transportation Secretary

The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, the union representing FAA safety employees, said the issue was isolated to two routers that were updated on Friday, and an official told Reuters the routers were believed to be in Arkansas and Texas. The union said its technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop, and an FAA official said the agency had conducted a safety assessment before the work. L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and was supporting the FAA's investigation; its shares last traded down about 4% after hours on Friday. The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to check for any further risks. The failure had initially prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday while agencies checked for a cyberattack; officials said they found no evidence of one.

A $50 billion argument over ageing systems

Friday's shutdown is the most dramatic sign yet of strain on an air traffic control system beset by ageing technology and a shortage of several thousand controllers. Duffy on Friday called for $50 billion to upgrade the system, up from his earlier request of $30 billion, after Congress approved $12.5 billion last year. House Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News on Saturday that he supports approving more funding this year. Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, the Democrats slated to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and its aviation subcommittee next year, said in a joint statement on Saturday that their panels would "hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again." They said the Transportation Department has awarded contracts worth $4.3 billion since receiving the $12.5 billion but has spent only $1 billion so far.

What to do if you are flying Sunday

Bedford's late-Sunday recovery timeline means Sunday morning departures remain exposed, with 875 Sunday flights already cancelled before the day began. If you are booked to fly in the US on Sunday: check your flight status in the airline's app before leaving for the airport, and if your flight is cancelled, use the travel waiver your airline has issued to rebook for a later date without extra cost rather than joining the airport queue. Travellers connecting onward to India should check the long-haul leg separately — Air India said its US services ran on schedule through the ground stop, but US domestic connections feeding those flights are where the cancellations are concentrated.
